questions.q: According to Section 1 of the IRR, what is the complete short title of the Act?
questions.n: Section 1 explicitly states that the Act shall be known as 'The Architecture Act of 2004'.

questions.q: Section 2 states that the State recognizes the importance of architects in what specific endeavor?
questions.n: The State policy emphasizes the role of professionals in nation-building and development.

questions.q: Based on Section 3, who is a person professionally and academically qualified, registered, and licensed under RA 9266?
questions.n: Section 3(1) defines an 'Architect' specifically as someone registered and licensed under this Act.

questions.q: How does Section 3 define the 'Scope of the Practice of Architecture'?
o: Strictly limited to the drawing of floor plans and perspectives.

Encompassing the provision of professional services in connection with site, physical and planning and the design, construction, enlargement, conservation, renovation, remodeling, restoration or alteration of a building or group of buildings.
Exclusively the structural design of bridges and dams.
The act of selling construction materials and hardware.
questions.n: This comprehensive description matches the definition found in Section 3(4) regarding architectural services.

questions.q: What is an 'Architect-of-record' according to the definitions in Section 3?
o: A government official who keeps a record of all architects.
The foreign architect who provided the initial concept.
The architect who only visits the site once a month.
The architect registered and licensed who is directly and professionally responsible for the total design of the project and who shall assume the civil liability for the plans.
questions.n: Section 3(5) defines the Architect-of-record as the person responsible for the design and the resulting civil liability.

questions.q: Under Section 3, which term refers to the intellectual property of the Architect regarding the plans, specifications, and design of a building?
questions.n: Section 3(12) defines these as instruments of service that remain the property of the architect.

questions.q: What is the primary difference between an 'Architect-of-record' and an 'Architect-in-charge of construction'?
o: There is no difference; they are interchangeable terms.
One must be a Filipino citizen, while the other can be a foreigner.
One is liable for the design, while the other is liable for construction supervision.
One works for the government, while the other works for a private firm.
questions.n: Sections 3(5) and 3(6) distinguish these roles based on design responsibility versus site supervision responsibility.

questions.q: Section 3(11) defines the 'Commission'. To which body is it referring?
o: National Commission for Culture and the Arts (NCCA)
questions.n: The law defines 'Commission' as the PRC, which oversees all professional boards in the country.

questions.q: According to the Statement of Policy, the State aims to protect the public from 'unprofessional, unethical, immoral, or incompetent' practice through what?
o: Strict price controls on design fees
questions.n: Section 2 identifies the regulation of practice through licensure as the primary mechanism for public protection.

questions.q: Which of the following is included in the definition of 'Planning' under Section 3(15)?
o: Only the financial auditing of a construction project.
The marketing and sale of subdivided lots.
Physical, social, and economic aspects of land and site development.
Solely the mechanical and electrical layouts.
questions.n: The IRR definition encompasses the broader multi-disciplinary approach to land use and site preparation.

questions.q: The term 'Consulting Architect' refers to an architect with:
o: A fresh graduate who provides advice to classmates.
Specialized knowledge and exceptional professional experience in a particular field of architecture.
An architect who does not have a license but works in a firm.
Any architect who is currently unemployed.
questions.n: Section 3(7) defines the consultant as an expert who provides advice in a specific area of expertise.

questions.q: What is the legal name for a sole proprietorship, partnership, or corporation registered with the proper agencies for architectural practice?
questions.n: Section 3(14) defines the 'Architectural Company' as the legal entity through which practice is conducted.

questions.q: Under the definition of 'Architectural Firm' in Section 3, who must hold the majority of ownership or interest?
questions.n: The law requires that professional architectural firms be owned and controlled by registered professionals.

questions.q: What does Section 3(20) define as the documents that describe the technical details of the project, excluding the drawings?
questions.n: Specifications are the written descriptions of materials, standards, and workmanship requirements.

questions.q: Which term describes the 'physical planning' of a site or community as defined in Section 3(22)?
questions.n: Urban design is the specialized physical planning that deals with groups of buildings and public spaces.

questions.q: Under Section 3, 'Service Agreement' refers to a notarized written contract between:
questions.n: The service agreement is the formal contract establishing the professional relationship and fees.

questions.q: What is the 'Board of Architecture' responsible for according to the IRR?
o: Issuing building permits in every municipality.
Building physical infrastructure for the government.
Supervising the licensure examination and regulating architectural practice.
Providing free architectural services to the poor.
questions.n: The PRB is the administrative body created to implement RA 9266 under the PRC.

questions.q: Which of the following falls under 'Architectural Interior' as defined in Section 3(21)?
o: The design of the building's drainage system.
The landscaping of the exterior garden.
Detailed physical planning of architectural interiors including finishes and fixtures.
The structural calculation of the roof trusses.
questions.n: This involves the design and layout of elements within the building envelope as part of architecture.

questions.q: Section 3(25) defines 'Continuing Professional Development' (CPD) as:
o: A one-time seminar attended after graduation.
Sustained and progressive learning to maintain professional competence.
The initial 2-year internship before the board exam.
The act of retaking the licensure exam every year.
questions.n: CPD is the post-licensure requirement for architects to stay updated with new trends and laws.

questions.q: Who is defined as a person who holds a valid Certificate of Registration and a Professional Identification Card?
o: Foreign Architect with no local permit
questions.n: An RLA is someone who has officially passed the exam and maintains an active status with the PRC.

questions.q: In Section 3(27), what does 'Site Planning' involve?
o: Finding a location for a new office building.
The detailed physical planning of land for a specific project.
Calculating the total cost of construction materials.
The search for a new job in a different city.
questions.n: Site planning is the process of arranging structures and land use on a specific plot of land.

questions.q: What is 'Authorship' in the context of Section 3(32)?
o: The act of writing a textbook about architecture history.
The contractor who built the building according to the plans.
The unique and distinct creation by an architect through the use of design concepts and technical expertise.
The client who suggested the color of the walls.
questions.n: Authorship establishes the architect's legal claim to the original design as a creator.

questions.q: Which term describes the whole of the building's physical structure, including its form and spaces?
questions.n: Section 3(33) defines 'Architectural Works' as the resulting physical construction of the architect's design.

questions.q: According to Section 2, the State protects the public from which of the following practices?
questions.n: The State policy is to ensure that only competent and ethical professionals practice architecture.

questions.q: Under Section 3, 'Professional Practice' refers to:
o: The act of rendering services as defined by the law for compensation or otherwise.
Working as an unpaid volunteer in a construction site.
The pursuit of a Master's degree in Architecture.
Simply having the title 'Architect' on a business card.
questions.n: Practice is the active application of professional skills as governed by the IRR.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT explicitly listed in the State Policy (Section 2) as a quality the State shall develop in its pool of architects?
questions.n: The law specifies professionals should be 'technically virtuous' rather than just 'sufficient'.

questions.q: In the definition of 'Architect-of-record', what specific type of liability is the architect assuming for the plans and specifications?
questions.n: Section 3(5) specifically identifies civil liability as the responsibility of the Architect-of-record.

questions.q: Per Section 3(3), who is the 'Architect-in-charge of construction'?
o: The architect who signs the building permit
The architect liable for construction supervision
The general contractor of the project
questions.n: This role is defined by the professional responsibility and liability regarding site supervision.

questions.q: What does Section 3 define as the 'formal contract between the architect and client'?
questions.n: Section 3(30) defines this as the notarized written contract specifying the scope and fees.

questions.q: Which term refers to the 'conceptualization' and 'artistic' aspects of creating a building as defined in Section 3?
questions.n: Section 3(18) defines this as the artistic and conceptualizing phase of the architectural work.

questions.q: According to Section 3(9), what is the 'Duly Accredited Professional Organization'?
questions.n: The IAPOA is the specific organization accredited by the PRB and the Commission.

questions.q: How does Section 3 define 'Architectural Firm'?
o: A group of contractors working together on a project.
A non-profit foundation for heritage preservation.
A sole proprietorship, partnership or corporation registered to practice architecture.
The office of the local building official.
questions.n: This definition covers the various legal business structures allowed for architectural practice.

questions.q: Under Section 3, 'Structural Design' as performed by an architect is specifically in relation to:
questions.n: The definition in Section 3(16) limits the architect's scope of structural design to buildings.

questions.q: What is the 'Board' as defined in Section 3(10)?
o: The Provincial Board of the local government
The Board of Trustees of an architecture school
The Professional Regulatory Board of Architecture
The Board of Directors of the UAP
questions.n: The IRR uses 'Board' as a shorthand for the specific regulatory body of the profession.

questions.q: In the Statement of Policy (Section 2), the State aims to protect the public against 'unethical' practice. Which of the following is an example of an unethical practice?
o: Failing to pass the licensure exam on the first try.
Using a computer for drafting instead of manual drawing.
Charging a higher fee than a competitor.
Accepting commissions from a supplier without the client's knowledge.
questions.n: This represents a conflict of interest and a violation of the professional code of ethics.

questions.q: The definition of 'Site Planning' in Section 3(27) involves the detailed physical planning of land for a specific project. Who is responsible for this?
questions.n: Site planning is explicitly listed as part of the scope of architectural practice in Section 3.

questions.q: What is 'Consulting Architect' according to Section 3(7)?
o: A foreign architect working without a license.
An architect with specialized knowledge in a particular field of architecture.
A student doing an internship in a design firm.
questions.n: This role is defined by exceptional experience and expertise in a specific niche.

questions.q: Under Section 3(12), architectural documents like plans and specs are the intellectual property of whom?
o: The Client who paid for them
questions.n: The law clarifies that these instruments of service remain the property of the architect.

questions.q: What is the short title of RA 9266?
o: The Architect's Law of the Philippines
questions.n: This is the official short title designated in Section 1 of the law.

questions.q: Section 3(24) refers to IAPOA. What is the full meaning of this acronym?
o: Integrated and Accredited Professional Organization of Architects
Internal Agency for Professional Oversight of Architects
Institute of Architects and Planners of Asia
International Association of Philippine Operating Architects
questions.n: This is the official title defined in the IRR for the recognized professional body.

questions.q: According to Section 3(33), 'Architectural Works' includes which of the following?
o: The building itself, including its form and spaces.
The property tax assessment of the lot.
The financial budget of the client.
questions.n: This covers the physical manifestation of the architect's design.

questions.q: In Section 2, the State declares architecture to be 'vital to:'
questions.n: The policy statement links the profession directly to the growth of the country.

questions.q: Per Section 3(20), 'Specifications' describe the project's technical details. What is NOT typically found in a specification?
questions.n: Dimensions and layouts are found in the drawings, while specifications focus on written quality and methods.

questions.q: Section 3(15) defines 'Planning' as a multi-disciplinary activity. Which of the following is included in this activity?
o: Just the location of the plumbing vents
Only the color scheme of the interior
questions.n: The IRR definition recognizes that planning goes beyond just drawing and includes social/economic factors.

questions.q: What happens if an architect practices without a valid Certificate of Registration and a Professional Identification Card?
o: They can still practice as long as they have a diploma.
It is considered illegal practice of architecture.
They only need to pay a small fine to continue.
They can practice as long as they work for a licensed architect.
questions.n: RA 9266 mandates both documents for a person to legally identify as an architect and practice.
